title: Fiat Topolino: Small Italian Car, Huge Fun and Flair

body_markdown:
Between 1936 and 1955, Fiat sold more than 500,000 copies of the Topolino, an undeniably cute little car with a name that translates to “little mouse,” which also is the Italian name for Mickey Mouse.


Cute, but downright historic. Though comedian and car collector Jay Leno has an eye for horsepower, he also appreciates innovation, which the original Topolino certainly represented. “The Topolino was Italy’s answer to the Model T,” Leno told *Hemmings* , about his own 1937 Topolino, which came with a gasoline-powered four-cylinder engine that had 13 horsepower. “It really defines a period, how to take an economy where people have literally nothing, and engineer the least expensive, highest-mileage, yet stylish-looking thing you could design.”


That original Topolino was a rule-breaker—and the template for a great many vehicles over the next two decades.


Deremer Studios LLC


Fast-forward to another groundbreaker—this all-new, electric city car, appropriately named the Topolino. Fiat began producing it for the European market in 2023, and it came to the U.S. as a 2026 model, with updates for 2027.


It is, says parent company Stellantis, “fiercely adorable,” a remarkably apt description of a remarkable little car that can satisfy the daily transportation requirements of a great many Americans, especially those in, for example, beachside communities or resorts.

Deremer Studios LLC


Deremer Studios LLC


Deremer Studios LLC


Which is where we drove the Topolino—in Florida, at Lauderdale-by-the-Sea, part of Fort Lauderdale’s geography. Says its website: “If there was ever a Norman Rockwell-style painting done of a South Florida beach town, it would look like Lauderdale-By-The-Sea.” And on its roads today, artist Rockwell might certainly include a Topolino or two.


For 2027, the Fiat Topolino that is sold in the U.S. comes with a package that makes it street-legal as an LSV, or low-speed vehicle, governed by a speed limiter that allows the new Topolino to hit 25 mph, which it does quickly. The 2026 models can be retrofitted with a (free) kit that makes them LSV-legal, too. An LSV is legal to drive on roads that have a maximum speed limit of 35 mph.


Deremer Studios LLC


“The Fiat Topolino,” says the company, “brings its unmistakable Italian spirit to U.S. shores—playful, stylish and offering a new kind of freedom for modern neighborhoods.” In full agreement is Andrew Waterhouse, head of Fiat North America, who was on hand to answer questions about the Topolino. “We think the Fiat personality truly comes through with its design,” he said, a design that was, of course, penned in an Italian studio. Indeed, the styling on the Topolino reads clearly as a Fiat, as does a big FIAT badge on the nose.


Andrew Waterhouse


Deremer Studios LLC


Deremer Studios LLC


Deremer Studios LLC


So what is it like to drive? We sampled several 2027 Topolinos, and found a vehicle that is ideal for the tasks at hand. Power is more than ample for two aboard, and the front-wheel-drive Topolino is sure-footed, and benefits from actual car-sized 155/65R14 tires. The Topolino doesn’t require a pricey, dedicated home charger; it recharges to full strength using 110- or 220-volt household power while you sleep, in five to seven hours. The advertised range is 46 miles.


That’s plenty for a trip to the grocery store or a restaurant, particularly if you live in a community designed around the LSV experience, like Lauderdale-by-the-Sea. Over several sun-drenched hours of test driving Topolinos, we never once felt challenged by bigger vehicles, nor did we ever feel like we needed one.


Deremer Studios LLC


Topolino Open Air


Deremer Studios LLC


Topolino Dolce Vita


Deremer Studios LLC


New for 2027 is the Topolino Open Air, which has a lovely roll-back soft top like the existing Dolce Vita model, introduced last year. The Open Air comes with full doors, while the Dolce Vita is a step-in model, with what Fiat calls “rope doors,” which are clip-on twisted ropes. Factory seat belts, of course, keep you snug in seats that were far more comfortable than we were expecting. “Dolce Vita” is, of course, Italian for “the sweet life,” a sensation enhanced by the open-air feel it provides.


Verde Vita Mint


Stellantis


Corallo Orange


Stellantis


Luna Greige


Stellantis


It is likely by design that the Topolino’s vivid colors—Verde Vita Mint, Corallo Orange, and Luna Greige—add to its visibility. And that visibility seemed to attract people who, at stoplights, asked what we were driving and commented on its attractiveness. (The Verde Vita Mint got the most compliments, and was our favorite color, as well.)


Deremer Studios LLC


Fiat has a number of aftermarket options available for the Topolinio, including an accessory called Monsterlino, which will be offered shortly. It comes from respected audio brand Monster, and it’s described as a “grab-and-go audio system with stereo Bluetooth speakers that magnetically attach to the car, then snap onto one’s phone so the music goes wherever they go.” It will be available at[Fiatusa.com](https://fiatusa.com/) .


That site is also a good source to learn more about the Topolino, and the “find a dealer” feature is helpful, as only select U.S. Stellantis auto dealers have been commissioned to sell the Topolino. There is, by the way, free home delivery, up to 50 miles. For our location, as an example, the “finder” found five Topolino dealers within 50 miles of our front door.


As for the price? The Topolino starts at $13,995, and with shipping, that comes to just under $15,000. Dealers can offer advice on insuring a Topolino, as well as financing options.


Deremer Studios LLC


Slightly more suntanned than we were when we began, our afternoon test-driving Topolinos confirmed that a solid LSV like this has a place among transportation options. As we dropped that Mint Topolino off at the hotel’s valet parking, a couple walking by inspected it closely. “Adorable,” she said. Sadly, she wasn’t talking about us.


There are other LSVs, but none with this Italian flavor and fun. And the Topolino is the only one that says FIAT up front.
